title: Wide-bandgap semiconductor cost scaling
bottleneck: Gallium nitride and silicon carbide outperform silicon in power electronics (EVs, grid, data-center power), but substrates are expensive, defect densities high, and GaN-on-silicon integration still trails native substrates in performance. SiC wafer costs remain multiples of silicon, and scaling to larger wafers is slow. Cost, not performance, blocks adoption in price-sensitive applications.
why_it_blocks: Power conversion losses waste a significant share of global electricity; cheap wide-bandgap devices would cut those losses across transport and grid. High cost confines the efficiency gains to premium applications, slowing decarbonization of power electronics.
current_state: SiC is ramping in EVs with 200mm wafers in production, and GaN is established in fast chargers. Continued cost reduction toward silicon parity is the unresolved challenge. Substrate quality varies between suppliers, so device makers must qualify each source, slowing cost learning.
